title: A rewrite of one notes line cannot drop a sentence that is still true
why: Twice today a rewrite or fold of a docs/debts/notes.md line dropped one sentence that was still true (#1958 d4163eceb, #2002 6c8b057cb). Each time a haiku fix check caught it and forced a new review chain (timing-tests lane, session_013NEJL1jPC89ae6X6Pa4jmf, 08:19 CST Nov 8). A true limit can vanish from the debt store, and the lane pays a full re-review.
note: Check idea: when a commit removes a note line and adds one under the same or a folding id, list each removed sentence with no close match in the added lines, and require a Drops-lines reason that names it. Today the silent-undo check takes one trailer for the whole file. Home: the lost-lines part of lint/check_silent_undo.py, not revived_notes (lane lint-uses-pinned-tools, 08:23 CST Nov 8). Not part of notes-trailer-per-slug, which judges whole notes by slug. Done check: a red test where a rewritten note line that drops a still-present sentence, with no Drops-lines reason naming it, fails. Build lane. Filed by triage 08:22 CST Nov 8. Sent by the coordinator 08:24 CST Nov 8 to lane lint-uses-pinned-tools (session_013NEJL1N3YkCMouc1pELXyu), with its open silent-undo follow-up on #1973. Back to ready 07:22 CST Nov 12 (coordinator yes 07:21 CST): no live lane (was archived, handoff at handoffs/session_013NEJL1N3YkCMouc1pELXyu.md on archive/session-handoffs-2026-11-10).
